claims.text: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 has a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
The untreated alloy has poor mechanical integrity and forms cracks under mechanical loading.
A controlled thermal-mechanical treatment can induce a dual-phase precipitate-containing microstructure in the target alloy.
Minor compositional tuning can regulate the phase fraction and distribution in the target alloy.
The proposed processing will produce a finely dispersed secondary phase specifically along grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary secondary phase will be both ductile and coherent with the primary caloric phase.
The secondary phase will act as a crack deflector.
Interrupting and deflecting crack propagation will enhance toughness and resistance to cracking.
The dual-phase microstructure will increase the compressive strength of the target alloy.
Coherency of the precipitates will minimize disruption of the caloric phase transition.
The treated alloy will surpass 218 MPa in compressive strength.
The treated alloy will have a caloric response comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The mechanical benefit and retained caloric response will persist during cyclic applied-field and pressure-field operation near the caloric transition.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis presents thermal-mechanical processing as the single intervention, whereas the intervention field allows thermal-mechanical treatment and/or minor compositional tuning, leaving the proposed intervention non-unique.
